chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever says 'Glory be to God (subhan Allah)', God will plant a tree for him in Paradise due to it. Whoever says 'Praise be to God (alhamdulillah)', God will plant a tree for him in Paradise due to it. Whoever says 'There is no god but God (la ilaha illa Allah)', God will plant a tree for him in Paradise due to it. Whoever says 'God is the Greatest (Allahu akbar)', God will plant a tree for him in Paradise due to it.
Then a man from Quraysh said: O Messenger of God, then we have many trees in Paradise! He said: Yes, but beware of sending fires upon them to burn them. For God, Mighty and Majestic, says:
O you who have believed, obey God and obey the Messenger, and do not invalidate your deeds.

key_terms.الحمد لله: Alhamdulillah — Praise be to God; a form of tahmid (praise)
key_terms.الله أكبر: Allahu akbar — God is the Greatest; a form of takbir (magnification)
key_terms.تبطلوا أعمالكم: To invalidate/nullify your deeds — a grave warning about losing spiritual merit through disobedience
key_terms.سبحان الله: Subhanallah — Glory be to God; a form of tasbih (glorification)
key_terms.لا إله إلا الله: La ilaha illallah — There is no god but God; the declaration of divine unity (tahlil)

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say about saying subhanallah, alhamdulillah, la ilaha illallah, and Allahu akbar?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) linked the four great remembrances (tasbih, tahmid, tahlil, takbir) to earning trees in Paradise. When a companion from Quraysh expressed joy at the abundance of such trees, the Prophet immediately cautioned that sins and disobedience to God and His Messenger act like fire that can burn down all those spiritual trees. The hadith concludes with Quran 47:33, underscoring that good deeds can be nullified by failing to obey divine commands.
